analysis:
The only change is in .github/workflows/ci.yml, in the test-provider job. It adds one CI step, 'Run isolated native MiMo lifecycle drain gate', after the retained-fault gate near base line 360. The step runs scripts/run-nested-suite.sh with testGracefulDrainAfterServedRequestRetiresNativeOwnerWithinDeadline --no-parallel. Environment: MIMO_V26_SERIAL_NATIVE_TESTS=1, MIMO_V26_PROVIDER_LIFETIME_NATIVE_TESTS=1, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=0. Guard: !cancelled() with the provider-ci-build and mimo-fixtures steps succeeded. timeout-minutes is 5. This mirrors the existing retained-fault step.

Security review: no new secrets, permissions, triggers or third-party actions. There are no untrusted-input interpolations; the run string is a fixed literal. The prefix-cache kill switch is set to 0, which matches T-041's DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 posture and only disables the SSD cache in the test process, so no at-rest artifact is created. The change adds test coverage only; it touches no coordinator, provider, attestation or App Attest code and does not alter any threat model assumption. Remaining risk: the test body is not visible in this diff, so whether the named test exists or is non-vacuous depends on run-nested-suite.sh tripwires. That is a CI-quality concern, not a security regression. No cross-file security interactions need follow-up.
